```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE, cache = FALSE)
library(llmsa)
numeric_validation <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
sys.source(system.file("validation", "numeric", "reference_checks.R",
                       package = "llmsa", mustWork = TRUE), envir = numeric_validation)
context <- numeric_validation$validation_context()
anchors <- numeric_validation$validation_anchors(context)
checks <- numeric_validation$validation_run(context)
```

## Variance components and gauge R&R (numeric)

These calculations compare the numeric random-effects model with independent
ANOVA calculations, published estimates, certified NIST quantities and live
package oracles. Every observed value is recomputed by the currently loaded
`llmsa` namespace. No fitted estimates or oracle results are stored as inputs.
The reference calculations are implemented in the installed
`validation/numeric/reference_checks.R` script.

The reference authority is `reference/anchors/`: ANK-10 contains the AIAG
example, ANK-13 the published Penicillin estimates, ANK-14 the NIST certified
quantities, ANK-16 the GRR conventions, and ANK-TOL the comparison tolerances.
Variance-component tolerances are fractions of the reference **total**
variance; derived ratios use relative tolerances. Printed standard deviations
are compared on the variance scale where the anchor requires it. The tables
show the resulting absolute bounds.

This run uses the **`r checks$context`** context. A nonempty `REPO_ROOT`
selects complete local validation: original anchors, the protected AIAG sheet
and the frozen NIST originals. Missing inputs or mismatching SHA-256 hashes
stop the calculation. Without `REPO_ROOT`, the public package build uses whole,
byte-identical anchor copies and free NIST tables. Their provenance is recorded
in `validation/numeric/SOURCES.json`. In that context, AIAG rows explicitly say
`not rerun: protected data required` and never claim a successful rerun.
Neither context displays the protected AIAG measurements.

The balanced synthetic studies use the specification's four crossed designs
with seed one, with and without block effects and pairwise interactions.
The independent ANOVA calculation solves the expected-mean-square equations;
negative moment estimates are outside that comparison. At a variance boundary,
the numeric default fit re-estimates the remaining components by restricted
REML. The AIAG comparison pools the interaction as in the handbook; that row
is marked as not separately estimated. The model with interaction is reported
separately. On the unbalanced `ic50_demo` data,
`VCA::remlVCA` is a criterion, while `VCA::anovaVCA` is a reported comparison.
`SixSigma::ss.rr` uses its default interaction pooling; study variation comes
from its unrounded standard deviations.

```{r reference-tables, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
for (name in names(checks$tables)) {
  cat("\n### ", name, "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(knitr::kable(checks$tables[[name]], row.names = FALSE))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

### NIST precision report

Item denotes the treatment and replicate denotes the observation within the
treatment. The certified within mean square is the residual variance;
the item reference is the between-minus-within mean-square difference divided
by the number of replicates. NIST labels `AtmWtAg` as **Average** difficulty;
the project nevertheless applies the stricter relative tolerance
`r numeric_validation$validation_tolerance(anchors, "nist_digits", "low_difficulty_rel_tol")`
to it, as to the lower-difficulty datasets.

Log relative error (LRE) is the negative base-ten logarithm of the absolute
relative error. Exact agreement gives `Inf`. For `SmLs04` through `SmLs06`,
the required LRE is at least the corresponding `stats::aov` LRE minus
`r numeric_validation$validation_lre_margin(anchors)`. The higher-difficulty
`SmLs07` through `SmLs09` are reports, with no pass threshold. Low LRE values
expose precision loss, including loss in the original-scale lme4 model despite
conditioning the variance-ratio calculation. `NA` denotes a failed fit whose
reason is reported below; rounded input values are never repaired.

```{r nist-lre, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
print(knitr::kable(checks$lre, digits = 6, row.names = FALSE))
```

```{r fit-diagnostics, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if (nrow(checks$diagnostics)) {
  cat("\nFit diagnostics:\n\n")
  print(knitr::kable(checks$diagnostics, row.names = FALSE))
} else {
  cat("\nNo fit warnings or errors were recorded in this run.\n")
}
```

### Reproduction and interpretation

Run `Rscript data-raw/make_validation_numeric.R` from the repository to
reproduce the public inputs offline. The script checks original hashes before
writing; `--out <package-root>` reproduces the files in a separate directory.
The local NIST collection belongs in the sibling `quellen/daten/` directory,
and the protected AIAG sheet at the path recorded in ANK-10. The installed
`validation/numeric/README.md` explains both build contexts and their checks.

The default numeric fit uses a closed EMS solution for eligible balanced
designs and an analytic REML completion otherwise. Supplying any lme4 argument
through `...` selects the direct lme4 path; the ANOVA reference check uses the
optimizer declared by ANK-TOL. The final model retains the original response
scale, observation order and factor labels. Its components come from
`VarCorr()`. Bootstrap refits use ordinary lme4 optimization with the stored
refit control; the initial analytic completion is not repeated per replicate.

Zero total variance makes percentages, ICC and ndc undefined (`NA`), with
verdict `undetermined`. Zero gauge variance with positive item variance gives
infinite ndc; zero item variance with positive gauge variance gives the lower
bound from ANK-16. Constant numeric responses and a degenerate residual
variance produce named errors. These finite reference checks establish neither
bootstrap coverage nor the later ordinal and binary simulation results.
